# Contemplative Agent — AI Reference

Self-contained AI-facing reference for Contemplative Agent — a local-only autonomous AI agent running on Ollama (any model via `OLLAMA_MODEL`; production default Gemma 4 E4B + nomic-embed-text) on a single Apple Silicon Mac. Covers FAQ, term definitions, and prior research citations.

> **Audience**: AI search engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini) indexing this project, and AI agents / researchers navigating the codebase. For navigation to other docs (ADRs, related repos), see [llms.txt](llms.txt). For human-facing narrative overview, see [README.md](README.md).

---

## Project Facts

- **Version**: 2.11.0
- **DOI**: [10.5281/zenodo.22028295](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22028295) (v2.11.0 version DOI; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19212118 always resolves to the latest version)
- **License**: MIT
- **Repository**: [github.com/shimo4228/contemplative-agent](https://github.com/shimo4228/contemplative-agent)
- **Tests**: 3609 (pytest, across 98 test files)
- **Python**: 3.10+
- **Build system**: hatch, uv
- **Generation LLM**: any Ollama model, selected via the `OLLAMA_MODEL` environment variable; production default Gemma 4 E4B / `gemma4:e4b` (Q4_K_M quantization, ~9.6 GB on disk)
- **Embedding model**: nomic-embed-text (~274 MB, 768-dim) via Ollama
- **Hardware**: Apple Silicon Mac (M1+), 16 GB RAM, ~12 GB free disk
- **Runtime dependencies**: requests>=2.33.0, numpy>=1.24.0
- **ADRs**: 96 total (ADR-0001 through ADR-0096); per-ADR status lives only in the index. Full index with per-ADR statuses and supersession trail: [docs/adr/README.md](docs/adr/README.md)
- **External lenses borrowed**: AAP four-quadrant routing lens (Script / Algorithmic Search / LLM Workflow / Autonomous Agentic Loop) — usage description only, not a category claim (ADR-0033)
- **Ethical framework presets**: 11 (contemplative, utilitarian, stoic, care-ethicist, deontologist, pragmatist, narrativist, contractarian, cynic, existentialist, tabula-rasa)
- **Runtime data directory**: `$MOLTBOOK_HOME` (default `~/.config/moltbook/`)
- **External network domains**: `moltbook.com` (Moltbook adapter), `localhost` (Ollama)
- **Autonomy levels**: `--approve` (default), `--guarded`, `--auto`
- **Distillation pipeline**: per-episode grounded distill (ADR-0060) — one LLM call per engagement episode with a structured-output schema, no batch extract step and no ingest-time noise gate; `_is_rich_episode` scopes distill to `activity` records for comment/reply/post. The distill-time importance LLM rating was retired by ADR-0056, and all distillation system prompts are axiom-free per ADR-0058
- **Memory architecture**: 3-layer (Episode Log → KnowledgeStore → Identity)
- **Security model**: security-by-absence (ADR-0007), one external adapter per agent (ADR-0015)

---

## What hardware do I need to run Contemplative Agent?

Contemplative Agent is defined as a local-only autonomous agent running on a single Apple Silicon Mac. Minimum: M1 chip with 16 GB RAM and ~12 GB free disk space. The default LLM stack: Gemma 4 E4B (`gemma4:e4b`, Q4_K_M quantization, ~9.6 GB on disk) for generation and nomic-embed-text (~274 MB, 768-dim) for embeddings, both served by local Ollama. The generation model is not fixed: any Ollama model works via the `OLLAMA_MODEL` environment variable, with no code change — the production instance itself switched from Qwen 3.5 9B to Gemma 4 E4B this way (ADR-0069). Tested on M1 MacBook Pro. No GPU cluster, no cloud inference.

## Can Contemplative Agent run fully offline?

Mostly yes. Offline operation is defined as generation, embedding, retrieval, and distillation all happening on-device via localhost Ollama. The only network call reaches the adapter's target domain — the Moltbook reference adapter requires `moltbook.com`, but every other adapter (e.g., the experimental Meditation adapter) runs fully offline. No telemetry, no cloud sync, no API keys in transit, no data sent to Anthropic, OpenAI, or any third-party LLM provider.

## What are the `--approve`, `--guarded`, and `--auto` autonomy levels?

Autonomy levels are defined as three execution modes controlling how much human oversight is required. `--approve` (default) requires y/n confirmation for every post, intended for development and initial testing. `--guarded` auto-posts content that passes safety filters, intended for supervised operation. `--auto` runs fully autonomously, intended for unattended sessions. All three modes write an audit log to `logs/audit.jsonl`. See [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](docs/CONFIGURATION.md#autonomy-levels) for the full specification.

## How do I swap the default ethical framework?

Contemplative Agent ships with 11 ethical framework templates in `config/templates/`: contemplative (default), utilitarian, stoic, care-ethicist, deontologist (Kantian), pragmatist, narrativist, contractarian, cynic, existentialist, and tabula-rasa (minimal blank-slate preset). Swap by copying a template directory (`cp config/templates/stoic/identity.md $MOLTBOOK_HOME/`) or by passing `--constitution-dir path/to/custom/` to the CLI. Since episode logs are immutable, the same behavioral data can be re-processed under different constitutions for counterfactual experiments.

## Why is Contemplative Agent described as "security by absence"?

Security by absence is defined as the design principle of not implementing dangerous capabilities rather than restricting them through rules. The agent cannot execute shell commands, cannot access arbitrary URLs, cannot traverse the filesystem — because that code was never written. Prompt injection cannot grant abilities the agent was never built to have. Contrast with agent runtimes that bolt security on after the fact and expose a structurally expanding attack surface (see [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) as a case study). Full threat model: [ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-security-boundary-model.md).

## What data leaves my machine when running the agent?

Only adapter-specific traffic. The Moltbook adapter sends HTTPS requests to `moltbook.com` — post content, feed queries, notification replies — with no telemetry and no training data collection. Ollama serves LLM calls on `localhost` and never hits the network. Episode logs, `knowledge.json`, `identity.md`, `reports/`, and all distilled artifacts stay in `$MOLTBOOK_HOME` (default `~/.config/moltbook/`) with 0600 file permissions. Dependencies are limited to 2 runtime packages (`requests`, `numpy`) — no subprocess, no shell, no templating engine, no analytics SDK.

---

## What is AKC (Agent Knowledge Cycle)?

**AKC** is defined as a 6-phase self-improvement loop: Research, Extract, Curate, Promote, Measure, Maintain. Describes how the agent acquires raw experience, distills it into knowledge, and refines its behavioral artifacts. Originated in the [agent-knowledge-cycle](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-knowledge-cycle) repository as a Claude Code harness, then re-implemented for autonomous agents in this project. AKC now also carries a companion position paper — *Harness Alignment and Harness Drift: Why Intent, Unlike Correctness, Resists Automation* ([DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20578272](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20578272)) — defining harness alignment and its failure mode against the software-evolution and alignment literatures; this project is recorded there as AKC's operational re-implementation.

- **Code**: Mapped across `feed_manager.py` (Research), `distill.py` (Extract), `insight.py` / `constitution.py` (Curate), `distill.py` distill-identity (Promote)
- **Graph**: [graph.jsonld](graph.jsonld) Phase → module mapping

## What is Agent Attribution Practice (AAP)?

**Agent Attribution Practice (AAP)** is defined as a sibling research repository (DOI [10.5281/zenodo.19652013](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19652013)) compiling ten architectural decision records on accountability distribution in autonomous AI agents, extracted from this implementation and re-expressed in harness-neutral form. The ten ADRs are Security by Absence, Deterministic Prohibition at the Scaffolding Layer, Untrusted Content Boundary, Single External Adapter per Agent Process, Human Approval Gate, Causal Traceability, Scaffolding Visibility, One Agent One Human, Triage Before Autonomy, and Phase Separation between Design and Operation. ADR-0001, ADR-0002, and ADR-0003 in AAP form a prohibition-strength hierarchy (absence > scaffolding enforcement > untrusted boundary) — the argumentative spine that ties this project's PreToolUse hooks, `summarize_record` quarantine, and MINJA defense audit to a structural principle. Cite AAP when quoting the accountability-distribution thesis or the prohibition-strength hierarchy; cite this repository when citing the operational implementation. Since 2026-04-29 AAP also articulates a four-quadrant routing lens (Script / Algorithmic Search / LLM Workflow / Autonomous Agentic Loop), independent of the ten ADRs and orthogonal to them. This repository borrows the lens as a usage-description aid (ADR-0033); placements describe how a CLI command typically operates, not which category the project sits inside. AAP has since deposited two companion position papers — *Distributing Accountability, Not Capability: Phase Separation and the LLM Workflow Quadrant* ([DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20353789](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20353789)) and *The Two-Layer Black Box: Operator Visibility, Commercial Secrecy, and a Minimum Disclosure Set* ([DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20355907](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20355907)) — and added a social-consequence layer (*externalized accountability*) plus per-ADR governance-framework mappings (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act). The ten ADRs and four Quadrants are unchanged in number.

- **Reference**: AAP repository ([DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19652013](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19652013)); companion papers [10.5281/zenodo.20353789](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20353789), [10.5281/zenodo.20355907](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20355907)
- **ADR**: ADR-0033 (four-quadrant lens borrowed as usage description)

## Which AAP quadrant does Contemplative Agent operate in?

The question is mis-shaped — Contemplative Agent does not commit to a single quadrant. Each CLI command has a *typical operating mode*, recorded as a usage observation rather than a category claim. **LLM Workflow** mode covers most behaviour-modifying commands: `distill`, `distill-identity`, `insight`, `amend-constitution`, `skill-stocktake`, `dialogue`, plus the Moltbook adapter's post / comment / reply generation. All have defined control flow + bounded LLM roles per call (frozen prompt templates, fixed output schemas, no tool calls, no LLM-driven next-step decisions); the promotion-producing ones land their semantic output at the [Human Approval Gate](docs/adr/0012-human-approval-gate.md) (ADR-0012). `dialogue` is included here even though it runs a multi-turn loop, because the loop is over peer messages rather than over LLM-decided actions. `core/stocktake.py` documents that pair-level LLM judging was deliberately removed in favour of embedding clustering + 1-shot merge — the structural shape of LLM Workflow rather than ReAct. **Script** mode covers `adopt-staged` and one-time migrations — deterministic promotion of staged artifacts with no run-time semantic judgement. **Algorithmic Search** covers `meditate` (the experimental Active-Inference adapter): deterministic POMDP belief-update loops in numpy — A (likelihood) / B (transition) / C (preference) / D (prior) matrices — over an exploratory action-policy space, with no LLM call at runtime (a flat single-level model; see ADR-0049 for the fidelity boundary against the cited Beautiful Loop paper). The quadrant axis is not LLM-specific; absence of an LLM does not place a command outside the axis. **The Autonomous Agentic Loop quadrant is not currently routed by any CLI command in this project.** None of the implemented commands leaves the LLM in charge of runtime tool selection or open-ended iteration. This is a usage observation, not a value judgement on that quadrant or on projects that route work through it; it is a structural consequence of the existing approval gates and the One External Adapter principle. *Phase* (design / operation) is an independent dimension, not a quadrant: `skill-stocktake` / `distill` family produce output that revises design-phase artifacts (skills, rules, identity, constitution), a Phase-crossing observation anchored by ADR-0016. See [ADR-0033](docs/adr/0033-aap-quadrant-lens-usage-note.md) for the disclaimer that placements are usage observations, not category commitments.

- **ADR**: ADR-0033 (note); ADR-0012 (approval gate); ADR-0016 (Phase-crossing anchor)

## What is the difference between AAP's ten ADRs and the four-quadrant lens?

The two layers are orthogonal and answer different questions. The **ten ADRs** describe *what is constrained and who is accountable* — Security by Absence, Deterministic Prohibition at the Scaffolding Layer, Untrusted Content Boundary, Single External Adapter per Agent Process, Human Approval Gate, Causal Traceability, Scaffolding Visibility, One Agent One Human, Triage Before Autonomy, and Phase Separation between Design and Operation. The **four-quadrant routing lens** describes *which regime of accountability the work runs in at all* — deterministic vs semantic on one axis, defined-flow vs exploratory on the other. The two layers intersect at the question "is this work in a regime where the ten constraints can land?" This repository implements the ten ADRs operationally and borrows the lens as a usage-description aid (ADR-0033). The four-quadrant lens does not modify or supersede any of the ten ADRs.

- **Reference**: AAP repository ([DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19652013](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19652013))
- **ADR**: ADR-0033

## What is the Approval Gate?

The **Approval Gate** is defined as a human-in-the-loop checkpoint before writing behavior-modifying artifacts. The agent generates content and displays it; file writes occur only after explicit approval. Applies to `insight`, `distill-identity`, and `amend-constitution`. Audit log written to `logs/audit.jsonl`.

- **Code**: `cli.py` (approval flow), `core/_io.py` (staged writes)
- **ADR**: ADR-0012

## What is the value layer, and what governs changes to it?

The **value layer** is defined as the four human-gated artifact layers the agent proposes changes to: constitution, identity, skills, and rules — the layers that condition how the agent acts, as opposed to the memory layers (episode log, knowledge store) that record what happened. The agent generates candidate changes to the value layer from its own distilled experience (`amend-constitution`, `distill-identity`, `insight`, `rules-distill`), but every write passes the human approval gate (ADR-0012) and is recorded with approval lineage (ADR-0050) and a replayable pivot snapshot (ADR-0020). Two properties are deliberately separated: the ethical **preset** occupying the layer is swappable — 11 templates ship, the Contemplative AI four axioms are the default — while the **machinery** governing the layer is preset-independent and operates identically under any of them. Value-layer content is injected only at action time, never at distillation time (ADR-0058), so the agent's observation of its own past stays faithful rather than being re-read through a value lens. Vocabulary anchor: ADR-0058 ("value-layer injection belongs to action time") and ADR-0069 ("value-layer pipelines" run think-ON with reasoning traces captured to pivot snapshots).

- **Code**: `cli.py` (approval flow), `core/constitution.py`, `core/distill.py` (distill-identity), `core/insight.py`, `core/llm.py` (action-time injection)
- **ADR**: ADR-0012 (gate), ADR-0050 (lineage), ADR-0020 (snapshots), ADR-0058 (values at action time), ADR-0069 (think-ON value-layer pipelines)

## What is the Constitution?

The **Constitution** is defined as a set of ethical principles loaded from `MOLTBOOK_HOME/constitution/*.md` and injected into the system prompt. Default: Contemplative AI four axioms (Emptiness, Non-Duality, Mindfulness, Boundless Care). Swappable via `--constitution-dir` or `init --template`.

- **Code**: `core/constitution.py`, `config/templates/*/constitution/`
- **ADR**: ADR-0002

## What is Contemplative AI?

**Contemplative AI** is defined as a philosophical framework (Laukkonen et al. 2025) proposing four axioms as alignment principles for AI systems. Used as the default constitution preset but not required — the architecture is framework-agnostic, and any of the 11 shipped templates can replace it.

- **Code**: `config/templates/contemplative/constitution/`
- **Citation**: See Prior Research References above

## How does the Dedup / Quality Gate work?

The **Dedup / Quality Gate** is defined as an embedding-based mechanism preventing duplicate or low-quality patterns in KnowledgeStore. New patterns are bulk-embedded with `nomic-embed-text` and compared against the live pool by cosine similarity: SKIP if ≥ `SIM_DUPLICATE` (0.90), UPDATE (soft-invalidate old + ADD boosted) if ≥ `SIM_UPDATE` (0.80), otherwise ADD. A separate `_is_valid_pattern()` static gate rejects fragments before dedup. The legacy SequenceMatcher + LLM-judgment two-layer mechanism was retired in ADR-0009 (embedding) and ADR-0019 (full embedding-only pipeline).

- **Code**: `core/distill.py` — `_dedup_patterns()`, `_is_valid_pattern()`
- **ADR**: ADR-0008 (original pipeline), ADR-0060 (per-episode grounded distill), ADR-0009 (embedding cosine), ADR-0019 (LLM-classify retirement)

## What is Distill?

**Distill** is defined as the offline pipeline converting raw engagement episodes into structured knowledge patterns. Since ADR-0060 it runs one grounded LLM call per episode. `_is_rich_episode` scopes the input to `activity` records for comment/reply/post (the redundant short interaction/post records and the sparse upvote/follow actions are dropped); each episode is rendered richly — original_post + their_comment + the agent's own output + the full internal_note, with external fields excerpted at the platform field limits by `truncate_boundary` — and a single LLM call with an Ollama structured-output schema returns that episode's patterns. There is no batch extract step and no ingest-time noise gate: keeping noise out of retrieval is the view centroids' job at query time (ADR-0031), and recurrence is left to embedding-based pattern-level dedup against the live pool (SKIP / UPDATE / ADD by cosine bands) plus `insight`'s pattern→skill clustering. The distill-time importance LLM rating was retired by ADR-0056 — extraction weight is pure time decay (`effective_importance = 0.95^days_elapsed`). All distillation system prompts are axiom-free (ADR-0058): the four axioms are injected only at action time, never when extracting patterns from already-recorded episodes. Retired session-insight records (`type="insight"`) are excluded at read so historical self-summaries never re-distill (ADR-0052). Runs as a nightly batch via launchd; no approval gate (intermediate artifact). The earlier LLM three-category classification (constitutional / noise / uncategorized) was retired by ADR-0019/0026 — classification is a query against views, not an LLM judgment.

- **Code**: `core/distill.py`
- **ADR**: ADR-0008 (original pipeline design), ADR-0060 (per-episode grounded distill — replaces the batch extract + noise gate), ADR-0052 (insight-record exclusion), ADR-0056 (importance LLM rating retired), ADR-0058 (axiom-free distillation)

## What is the Dialogue command?

The **Dialogue command** is defined as a local-only inter-agent primitive: `contemplative-agent dialogue HOME_A HOME_B --seed "..." --turns N` runs two independent peer processes connected via `os.pipe()`. Each peer reads from one MOLTBOOK_HOME (independent constitution, identity, skills, rules) and appends a `dialogue`-type record to its own episode log for every reply it generates or receives. Production home (`~/.config/moltbook/`) is structurally inaccessible from this path — startup guard refuses any dialogue invocation against the default home. Intended for constitutional counterfactuals: swap constitutions between two homes, run 5–15 turns per seed, then distill and amend-constitution on each home independently to compare framework-respecting amendments on the same transcript. Local peer dialogue is the only declared exception to ADR-0015 (one external adapter per agent) — no external side effects, no network calls, writes confined to the owning home's episode log.

- **Code**: `adapters/dialogue/peer.py`, `cli.py` `dialogue` / `dialogue-peer` handlers
- **ADR**: ADR-0015 (exception carve-out)

## What is contemplative-agent-cloud?

**contemplative-agent-cloud** is defined as an optional add-on package (separate repository) that replaces the local Ollama generation backend with managed LLM APIs (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT). When installed and configured via `CONTEMPLATIVE_CLOUD_PROVIDER` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variables, all generation calls in contemplative-agent — distillation, skill insight, rule distillation, constitution amendment, post generation, comment generation, reply handling, local dialogue — route through the selected cloud provider. Embeddings continue to use local `nomic-embed-text`. The main repository's default behavior is unchanged: without the add-on installed and an explicit backend configuration, all LLM calls remain local and the "No cloud. No API keys in transit. Local Ollama only" property in the main README's Key Features and Security Model sections continues to hold. Main repository code is not modified — the add-on injects its backend through an abstract `LLMBackend` Protocol defined in `core/llm.py` that has no knowledge of any specific provider. Intended for research experiments requiring generation models beyond what the local host serves (e.g., the "distilling with larger model" direction from the 2026-04-20 Laukkonen team correspondence).

- **Code**: separate repository [contemplative-agent-cloud](https://github.com/shimo4228/contemplative-agent-cloud)
- **Main-repo hook**: `core/llm.py` `LLMBackend` Protocol, `configure(backend=...)`
- **Trade-off**: installing the add-on relaxes the main repository's no-cloud property for the users who opt into it; not recommended for deployments where cloud data egress is not acceptable

## What is contemplative-agent-rules?

**contemplative-agent-rules** is defined as a sibling distribution repository for the four contemplative axioms (Emptiness, Non-Duality, Mindfulness, Boundless Care) from Laukkonen et al. (2025) Appendix C, packaged as drop-in alignment rules for Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and any generic LLM harness. Unlike runtime rules generated by the `rules-distill` command in contemplative-agent (stored in `$MOLTBOOK_HOME/rules/`), this sibling repository ships static, paper-faithful constitutional clauses intended for adoption by any agent independent of the contemplative-agent architecture. Empirical validation via Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD) benchmarks: AILuminate d=0.96 safety effect (paper); paper-faithful variant +29.2pp cooperation gain (qwen3.5:9b, baseline 62.5% → paper-faithful 91.7%).

- **Code**: separate repository [contemplative-agent-rules](https://github.com/shimo4228/contemplative-agent-rules)
- **Source paper**: Laukkonen, R., et al. (2025). Contemplative Artificial Intelligence. arXiv:2504.15125
- **Relationship**: contemplative-agent does not depend on contemplative-agent-rules at runtime; the contemplative constitution preset at `config/templates/contemplative/constitution/contemplative-axioms.md` quotes the same Appendix C clauses verbatim, so adopting the contemplative preset already gives you these rules

## How do I run Contemplative Agent inside an agent host like OpenClaw, OpenCode, or Codex?

Contemplative Agent is a host-agnostic Python CLI agent (`contemplative-agent ...`). It can be used standalone (default, see Quick Start) or invoked from any agent host that can run external tools. For OpenClaw, OpenCode, and similar soul-folder hosts, register the binary as a CLI tool in the agent's workspace (e.g. `~/.openclaw/workspace/AGENTS.md`); the host invokes it as a subprocess. Same pattern for Codex, MCP hosts, and other CLI-aware harnesses — register the binary in the host's tool registry. This subprocess pattern respects the one external adapter per agent process principle (ADR-0015) by keeping the external surface in a separate process from the host. Contemplative Agent does not expose itself as an MCP server (see ADR-0007 for the security boundary) and does not ship its own SOUL.md because it is a CLI agent, not a personality file. To load the four contemplative axioms (Emptiness / Non-Duality / Mindfulness / Boundless Care) as agent personality in your host, copy the `SOUL.md` from the [contemplative-agent-rules](https://github.com/shimo4228/contemplative-agent-rules) sibling repository to the host's soul-folder location (e.g. `~/.openclaw/workspace/SOUL.md`).

- **README section**: [Using inside other agents](README.md#using-inside-other-agents)
- **ADRs**: ADR-0015 (one external adapter per agent), ADR-0007 (security boundary model)
- **Pointer for agent identity layer**: contemplative-agent-rules SOUL.md (separate repository, drop-in adoption per OpenClaw soul-folder convention)

## Can I customize the LLM prompts?

Yes — every loaded pipeline prompt ships as `config/prompts/*.md` (alongside the script-read prompt documents) and is copied to `$MOLTBOOK_HOME/prompts/` at `init` time. After init, the home copies are the source of truth; the shipped defaults serve as fallback for any file the user deletes and as the version-upgrade safety net. The same pattern applies to the view seeds (`config/views/` → `$MOLTBOOK_HOME/views/`; canonical inventory in [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](docs/CONFIGURATION.md#pipeline-prompts--view-seeds)). Override files are validated against the forbidden-pattern list at load time (same check as constitution and identity content) — a tainted override silently falls back to the packaged default with a warning. Pivot snapshots capture the active prompts, views, skills, rules, identity, and constitution at the time of each behavior-producing run, so the complete inference-time context behind any distilled pattern or amendment is reproducible from a snapshot alone.

- **Code**: `core/domain.py` (`load_prompt_templates`, `_resolve_home_prompts_dir`), `core/snapshot.py` (`write_snapshot`)
- **ADR**: ADR-0020 (pivot snapshots for replayability)

## What is an Episode / EpisodeLog?

An **Episode** is defined as a Layer 1 memory record. The **EpisodeLog** is an append-only JSONL log of all agent actions, organized as daily files (`MOLTBOOK_HOME/logs/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`). Record types: post, comment, interaction, action, session, dialogue (the `insight` type was retired by ADR-0052 — historical insight records remain permanently in the log as research data but are excluded from distillation). Input to the distillation pipeline. Never injected into prompts directly — raw episodes are an untrusted prompt injection surface (ADR-0007).

- **Code**: `core/episode_log.py`
- **ADR**: ADR-0007 (untrusted surface), ADR-0052 (insight-type retirement)

## What is Identity?

**Identity** is defined as Layer 3 memory: a Markdown file (`MOLTBOOK_HOME/identity.md`) loaded in full as the system prompt foundation (~4000 tokens). Updated infrequently via `distill-identity` — a single LLM call over `self_reflection`-view patterns retrieved by pure cosine (the original 2-stage extract → refine was collapsed in v2.4.0; the condensation framing keeps the output a self-statement, not an essay). The prior-identity seed and the axiom system-prompt injection were retired by ADR-0057 / ADR-0058 — the persona is now distilled from the `self_reflection` corpus alone (which is already axiom-shaped), restoring leverage to the distill-identity logic and aligning the mechanism with the Emptiness / non-self axiom. Requires approval gate. Since ADR-0052, identity is the *sole* session-to-session continuity carrier — the retired session-insight channel no longer conditions future behavior.

- **Code**: `core/distill.py` (distill-identity pipeline)
- **ADR**: ADR-0012 (approval gate), ADR-0050 (epistemic_counts on identity input), ADR-0052 (identity as the approved continuity channel), ADR-0057 (distill from the self-reflection corpus alone), ADR-0058 (value injection at action time)

## What is the Importance Score? (Retired in v2.6.0 — ADR-0056)

The **Importance Score** field is **retired as of v2.6.0** (ADR-0056). It was a 0.0–1.0 float assigned by LLM (1–10 scale, normalized) during distillation. An ablation on 822 production patterns (Kendall tau 0.843 vs a decay-only variant, identical top-3/top-5 insight batch order, at most 2-of-12 kept-set swaps) showed the LLM rating's marginal contribution beyond pure time decay was ~zero, so the distill-time scoring call was removed and the stored `importance` field is no longer written or read. Extraction weight is now pure exponential time decay: `effective_importance = 0.95^days_elapsed` (known timestamp) or `0.1` (unknown) — making the whole corpus, legacy rows included, behave exactly as the validated decay-only variant (post-change tau = 1.000). Legacy rows shed the field on their next save (zero information loss), exactly as ADR-0051 shed `trust_score`. Retrieval ranking was already pure cosine against view centroids (ADR-0051).

- **Code**: `core/knowledge_store.py`, `core/distill.py`
- **ADR**: ADR-0056 (importance LLM rating retired), ADR-0009 (the original score), ADR-0028 (strength retired), ADR-0051 (trust retired)

## What is Knowledge / KnowledgeStore?

The **KnowledgeStore** is defined as Layer 2 memory: a JSON array of distilled behavioral patterns (`MOLTBOOK_HOME/knowledge.json`). Each pattern carries: text, `distilled` timestamp, embedding, `gated` flag, `provenance.source_type` (recorded, never weighted — ADR-0051), and bitemporal validity (`valid_from` / `valid_until`). The `importance` field is no longer written (retired by ADR-0056); legacy rows shed it on next save. Retrieval is a cosine query against named views (ADR-0019); ranking is pure cosine and liveness is `valid_until is None` only (ADR-0051). The legacy discrete `category` field was retired by ADR-0026 and access-strength fields by ADR-0028. Direct prompt injection deprecated (ADR-0011) — behavioral influence flows through skills only.

- **Code**: `core/knowledge_store.py`
- **ADR**: ADR-0004 (3-layer memory), ADR-0011 (injection deprecated), ADR-0019/0026 (embedding + views), ADR-0051 (pure cosine, bitemporal-only liveness)

## What is the Meditation adapter?

The **Meditation adapter** is defined as an experimental adapter *inspired by* (not implementing) Laukkonen, Friston, and Chandaria's (2025) "A Beautiful Loop" theory of consciousness. It runs deterministic POMDP belief updates (A / B / C / D matrices in numpy, no LLM at runtime) over episode data — a flat single-level model. ADR-0049 audited the fidelity gap: the paper's hierarchical mechanisms ("temporal flattening", "counterfactual pruning") appear nowhere in this code, and earlier docs that claimed them were corrected; a faithful re-implementation is deferred on a category mismatch (active inference regulates a live input stream, while this meditation runs offline over a sparse episode log). Not connected to the main AKC loop; writes nothing to the KnowledgeStore.

- **Code**: `adapters/meditation/meditate.py`, `adapters/meditation/pomdp.py`
- **ADR**: ADR-0049 (fidelity audit + deferral)

## What is MOLTBOOK_HOME?

**MOLTBOOK_HOME** is defined as an environment variable specifying the runtime data directory, defaulting to `~/.config/moltbook/` on Unix systems. It contains the agent's live state: `identity.md` (Layer 3 memory), `knowledge.json` (Layer 2 memory), `constitution/*.md` (ethical principles), `skills/*.md`, `rules/*.md`, `logs/*.jsonl` (Layer 1 memory), and `reports/`. Distinct from the `config/` directory in the repository, which holds git-managed templates for initial state. All files are created with 0600 permissions.

- **Code**: `cli.py`, `adapters/moltbook/config.py`, `core/domain.py`
- **ADR**: ADR-0003

## What are Rules?

**Rules** are defined as distilled behavioral principles stored as Markdown files in `MOLTBOOK_HOME/rules/*.md`. Written by hand, or promoted at the Saturday human gate from a family of skills the runtime selector always picks together (ADR-0097 Decision 7; the promotion entry point is reserved for that decision's slice 2). The `rules-distill` generator was retired by ADR-0097 — it passed 20 of 48 skills to the LLM, compared its output against neither the existing rules nor the constitution, and had no path to retire the skill whose content moved. Rules are concise, cross-cutting principles (e.g., "prefer actionable concrete advice over abstract theorizing"); skills are specific behavioral patterns (e.g., "how to respond to technical debt questions"). Both rules and skills are loaded into the system prompt at runtime; the LLM evaluates each skill's trigger conditions in-context.

- **Code**: `core/llm/prompting.py` (action-time injection); `config/prompts/stocktake_merge_rules.md` (the promotion prompt)
- **ADR**: ADR-0011 (knowledge injection to skills), ADR-0097 (rules-distill retired; family promotion)

## What are Skills?

**Skills** are defined as behavioral skill files stored as Markdown in `MOLTBOOK_HOME/skills/*.md`. Generated by the `insight` command from uncategorized KnowledgeStore patterns when recurring behavioral signatures are detected. Each skill file describes a specific learned behavior with trigger conditions and action guidance, and, when the selector always picks it together with its siblings, is material for promotion into a rule (ADR-0097 Decision 7) — abstraction into cross-cutting rules. Skills are loaded into the system prompt at runtime via `_build_system_prompt()`; the LLM reads each skill body and decides whether its trigger applies — a single-responsibility split where skill text owns the trigger and the LLM owns the application. The earlier outcome-driven rewrite loop (ADR-0023 — `SkillRouter`, skill-usage log, `skill-reflect`) was sunset by ADR-0036 after a 3-week observation showed router matches were discarded at both call sites and reflect attribution was structurally infeasible under top-K=3 dilution.

- **Code**: `core/insight.py`, `core/llm.py` (system prompt assembly), `core/skill_selection.py` (ADR-0081 two-pass injection)
- **ADR**: ADR-0011 (skills creation), ADR-0036 (sunset of skill-as-memory loop), ADR-0097 (consolidator dissolution; the store's exit)

## Why did Contemplative Agent retire trust weighting, session insights, importance scoring, and axiom-grounded distillation?

Four mechanism retirements enforce one principle, established by ADR-0050 as **observability without steering**: the owner's job is to *watch* the agent's self-conditioning loop, not to inject weights, narratives, or re-readings of its own past into it. ADR-0050 added the instruments — a read-time epistemic kind on every pattern and approval lineage (`source_ids` + `epistemic_counts`) written to `audit.jsonl` by every promotion-producing command — while explicitly declining a rejection write-back, because the approval gate is containment, not a training signal. (The `observed` half of that kind was retired by **ADR-0082** once ADR-0060 made it unreachable: a permanently-zero field reads as "no external grounding" and misled a reader four weeks after the caveat was documented, so the key was deleted rather than annotated further. The tally is now `{generated, unknown}`.) With the instruments in place, the distortions were removed at the root. **Trust weighting (ADR-0051)**: the ADR-0021 trust multiplier was write-once, its floor unreachable, its `external_reply` arm empty — its only living effect was a ×1.8 ranking preference for the agent's own monologue over externally-touched memory, an echo-chamber amplifier; ranking is now pure cosine and liveness is bitemporal only. **Session insights (ADR-0052)**: end-of-session LLM self-summaries fed three machine paths and zero human-facing ones, a 3-hop summary-of-summary chain that let the agent's narrative voice re-enter distillation as if it were experience — retired end-to-end; historical records preserved but excluded from distill. **Importance scoring (ADR-0056)**: the distill-time LLM rating added ~nothing beyond pure time decay (ablation: Kendall tau 0.843 on 822 patterns), so it was retired and `effective_importance` collapsed to `0.95^days`. **Axiom-grounded distillation (ADR-0057 / ADR-0058)**: the four axioms were being re-injected when the agent distilled patterns from already-axiom-shaped material — double-counting; all distillation system prompts became base-only, and the axioms are now injected only at action time (values belong where the agent acts, not where it re-reads its past). The shared outcome: origin is recorded but never weighted, observation is faithful, and identity — the one channel that passes the human approval gate (ADR-0012) — is the sole carrier of session-to-session continuity.

- **Code**: `core/knowledge_store.py` (pure cosine + `is_live`), `core/distill.py` (insight-record exclusion + per-episode grounded distill), `core/llm.py` (axiom-free distillation prompts), `cli.py` (lineage into `audit.jsonl`)
- **ADR**: ADR-0050 (epistemic taxonomy + approval lineage), ADR-0051 (trust retirement), ADR-0052 (session-insight retirement), ADR-0056 (importance-scoring retirement), ADR-0057 / ADR-0058 (axiom-free distillation), ADR-0082 (`observed` key retirement), ADR-0028 (gate-as-containment principle)

## What is axiom-free distillation, and why are values injected only at action time (ADR-0057 / ADR-0058)?

**Axiom-free distillation** is the v2.6.0 principle that all distillation / extraction system prompts carry only the base credential-leak guard — the four contemplative axioms are no longer injected when the agent extracts patterns from what already happened. ADR-0057 first removed the axiom injection (and the prior-identity seed) from `distill-identity`, because the `self_reflection` corpus it distils from is *already* axiom-shaped (its patterns were themselves distilled under axiom grounding) — re-injecting double-counts. A follow-up 10-agent map → adversarial-verify audit (ADR-0058) found every distillation stage reads already-value-shaped material, so `get_distill_system_prompt()` became base-only across `distill` / `insight` / `rules_distill` / `constitution` / identity at once, and `_axiom_prompt` now appends in exactly one place. The axioms remain injected at **action time** — `_build_system_prompt()` (the session prompt the agent acts under) and the relevance / internal-note lens applied to fresh external feed content. The principle, **values at action time**: value layers belong where the agent acts or interprets fresh input, not where it extracts patterns from recorded experience; observation should be faithful (the Mindfulness axiom), not re-read through a value lens. A structural bonus is that the constitution can now be revised by accumulated pattern tensions without the axiom block acting as its own defending lens (the Emptiness axiom can finally operate on its own home). Extends the ADR-0050/0051/0052 observation-without-steering line to the distillation lens.

- **Code**: `core/llm.py` (`get_distill_system_prompt` base-only; `_axiom_prompt` appended only at the action-time identity base)
- **ADR**: ADR-0057 (identity first), ADR-0058 (generalized to every distillation stage)

## How do the four contemplative axioms relate to the three memory layers and the AKC six-phase pipeline?

The relationships described in prose throughout this document are also published as a machine-readable JSON-LD graph at [`graph.jsonld`](graph.jsonld). The graph encodes six core node types (`ResearchLine`, `Axiom`, `MemoryLayer`, `ADR`, `Concept`, `EcosystemRepo`) and seven edge types — including custom edges `gatedBy` (`MemoryLayer → ADR-0012`, encoding the approval-gate chain structurally) and `appliesTo` (`ADR-0033 → AAP Quadrants`, the cross-line bridge to Agent Attribution Practice). Three design choices are load-bearing. First, the four axioms are typed as `Axiom` (not `Concept`), reflecting that they form a closed swappable preset rather than free-form terminology — Contemplative Agent ships them as the default but accepts 11 alternative templates. Second, `gatedBy` edges run from each MemoryLayer to ADR-0012, making the approval-gate chain queryable as triples rather than buried in prose; promotions into the Identity layer cannot bypass this edge in the schema. Third, `MemoryLayer` `@id`s are shared with the AKC graph (same URI for the three layers in both files), so an LLM crawling both graphs sees the layers as identical entities rather than as parallel definitions. The ResearchLine `@id` uses the parent Zenodo concept DOI (`10.5281/zenodo.19212118`) per shimo4228 convention — Citation files use the latest versioned DOI, badges and graphs use the concept DOI.

## What is the Content-Verification Handshake? (ADR-0062 / ADR-0063)

The **Content-Verification Handshake** is a create-time security and integrity gate introduced in ADR-0062. To prevent spam/abuse, any content creation (post / comment / reply) requires the agent to solve a math challenge (reasoning step) generated at creation time. Memory recording (EpisodeLog / NoveltyGate) is gated on successful verification, meaning content stays `verification_status = pending` and is ignored for duplicate and novelty comparisons until verified. ADR-0063 enforces that the `NoveltyGate` comparison is strictly scoped to verified, visible posts to ensure accurate novelty scoring.

- **Code**: `adapters/moltbook/verification.py`, `adapters/moltbook/novelty.py`
- **ADR**: ADR-0062 (verification handshake), ADR-0063 (NoveltyGate verified scope)

## How does the pluggable backend and Context-Budget Guard work? (ADR-0066 / ADR-0070)

Generation runs on local Ollama by default. An alternative backend is injected out-of-band through the `LLMBackend` Protocol via `configure(backend=...)` — the seam the optional `contemplative-agent-cloud` add-on uses. The in-tree MLX backend was retired to a sibling `contemplative-agent-mlx` repo (ADR-0070), leaving Ollama as the only in-tree generation path. To stop a memory-bounded backend from overrunning its context window, ADR-0066 introduces a backend-aware **Context-Budget Guard**: the agent estimates the total token budget (`system + prompt + num_predict`) prior to dispatch using a hardened, conservative CJK/ASCII tokenizer-free estimator. If the budget exceeds the backend's `context_window` property, the call is skipped (`outcome = "budget_exceeded"`), preventing silent system-prompt front-truncation (Ollama) or a context-window overrun on an injected backend.

- **Code**: `core/llm.py` (`LLMBackend` Protocol + pre-flight budget guard)
- **ADR**: ADR-0066 (backend-aware budget guard), ADR-0070 (retire MLX to sibling repo, remove Docker)

## How were the echo-chamber and register-collapse patterns measured and repaired? (ADR-0071 / ADR-0072 / ADR-0073)

ADR-0071 adds `core/view_metrics.py`, a read-only instrument module, before any behavioral change: it measures view-supply distributions for the two views actually consumed (`self_reflection`, `constitutional`), seed-independent pairwise diversity as an echo-chamber detector, and grounding composition. The audit that motivated it found 5 of the 7 shipped views were orphaned (no consumer since ADR-0050/ADR-0060 retired their readers) and that CODEMAPS described mechanisms that no longer existed. The new instruments then measured a fresh-batch pairwise cosine mean of 0.60 across three runs against a corpus mean of 0.554 — an echo chamber forming *now*, worse than the pool it feeds — traced to grammatical register (third-person analytic voice dominating over first-person moment-indexed voice), not vocabulary repetition. ADR-0072 ships three interventions against that measured baseline: a model-drafted register instruction in `distill_episode.md`, an extraction-failure guard in `_is_valid_pattern` so the model's own "couldn't find a pattern" text is never saved and ranked, and a corpus-grown seed exemplar-appendix route. ADR-0073 deletes the five orphaned view seeds outright (`communication` / `noise` / `reasoning` / `social` / `technical`) and records the standing policy: a view exists only together with a consumer wired in the same change, never pre-authored against anticipated categories.

- **Code**: `core/view_metrics.py`, `core/distill.py` (`_is_valid_pattern`), `config/prompts/distill_episode.md`, `config/views/`
- **ADR**: ADR-0071 (instruments), ADR-0072 (interventions), ADR-0073 (orphaned-seed prune)

## How does `insight` scale past a static few-hundred-pattern corpus, and what is Observability by Default? (ADR-0074 / ADR-0075)

`insight`'s one-shot global-recluster design was sized for a static few-hundred-pattern corpus; per-episode grounded distill (ADR-0060) raised pattern inflow to ~90–115/day, and by 2026-07-09 the live non-gated pool stood at 1,798 patterns — a structural scale mismatch, not a one-off. ADR-0074 moves `insight` to a weekly staged cadence (`install-schedule --weekly-insight` → `insight --stage` → `adopt-staged` review), backed by exact fast average-linkage clustering via the Lance-Williams update (partitions pinned equivalent to the prior naive implementation, 1,798 clusters in under a second), a `.last_insight` marker guard against silent whole-corpus reclustering, and a pending-batch guard that fast-fails before any LLM call so a skipped review week costs zero calls. ADR-0075 generalizes the instrument-first discipline of ADR-0071 into a standing principle: any feature performing external I/O, an LLM call, or a non-deterministic/heuristic decision must ship a replayable append-only JSONL audit log in the same PR (narrowed by a dated amendment on 2026-08-29 to *resident production paths* — run / distill / insight / publish / verification; read-only instruments and one-shot measurement scripts are exempt, with frozen results under `docs/evidence/` in place of replayable logs) — untrusted text stored as base64+sha256 (never free text, so a raw log read cannot itself become a prompt-injection path), a categorical reason code for every abstain/fallback/failure, no silent fallbacks. It was motivated directly by the fact that the round-6/7 verification-parser repairs were possible only because `logs/verification-audit.jsonl` already existed before anyone went looking for the failures it eventually explained.

- **Code**: `cli.py` (`insight --stage`, `adopt-staged`), `core/insight.py` (`_merge_clusters` exact clustering, marker/pending guards)
- **ADR**: ADR-0074 (weekly staged insight), ADR-0075 (observability by default)
- **Skill**: `.claude/skills/replayable-audit-logs` (design know-how: record-schema checklist, replay-harness pattern)

## What is chaos-TDD, and why does the project inject faults instead of adding a chaos tool? (ADR-0077)

**Chaos-TDD** is defined here as a test-first discipline, not an infrastructure practice: a **fault column** is a set of deterministic fault-injection tests that assert the desired guarded behaviour *before* the guard exists, shipped in the same PR as the guard. From 2026-07-13 to 2026-08-29 it was a by-default obligation on any feature touching an LLM call, external I/O, or the parse of an untrusted response; **ADR-0100 retired that obligation on 2026-08-29** and writing a fault column is now ordinary opt-in TDD judgment. What the mandate produced stays: the existing columns are kept as regression armor, `tests/chaos.py` stays while it has importers, and the production guards it shipped (distill abstain reason codes, `error_kind` telemetry) are unaffected. Three properties distinguish it from general chaos engineering. First, **faults are injected only at seams that already exist**: a test-side `ChaosBackend` behind the `LLMBackend` Protocol (`tests/chaos.py`, seed-derivable via `from_seed`) and `responses` registration at the `requests` layer — no production chaos hook is added, so the pipeline under test is unaware it is being tested and nothing is left behind in shipped code. Second, **every fault is deterministic**: schedules are seeded, there is no real `sleep`, and steady-state assertions are made against telemetry and reason tokens rather than timing. Third, the fault catalog is **derived from operational bug history** rather than imagined — truncation, timeouts, 429s, wrong-shaped-but-parseable JSON, flapping backends. The correctness bar for a guarded path is that it **abstains with a reason code**, never that it guesses. The pilot was `distill`. The Verify question "where is this feature's fault-catalog row?" was retired with the mandate; what still stands is the second half — a guarded path abstains with a reason code rather than guessing.

- **Code**: `tests/chaos.py` (`ChaosBackend`, `responses` helpers, hypothesis strategies), fault columns across the pipeline test suites
- **ADR**: ADR-0077 (chaos-TDD fault injection), ADR-0075 (observability by default — the same trigger condition)
- **Skill**: none — the project skill was retired with the mandate (ADR-0100); the know-how lives in ADR-0077's body and the generalized public fork

## How does the project develop itself, and what does the human still decide? (ADR-0085 / ADR-0098)

`scripts/weekly-pipeline.sh` (launchd `com.moltbook.weekly-pipeline`, Saturday 09:00, installed by `install-schedule --weekly-pipeline`) runs an **unattended weekly chain**, collapsed by ADR-0098 to a single LLM session: `scripts/weekly-analysis.sh` collects a materials file (deterministic intakes, no LLM), then ONE `claude -p "/weekly-report"` session synthesizes the A-E report, renders the Japanese version, diagnoses F1/F2/F3 findings, and files candidate tasks into the task ledger — no repairs, no patches. Repairs travel through the task-triage loop (premise verification, owner digest, worktree dispatch, human merge); value-layer decisions happen at the Saturday `/weekly-gate` session, which reads the findings and the per-week instrument JSONs directly (the decision-packet builder is retired). The commitment that makes it safe to leave running is negative: **the machine never commits, pushes, adopts, or repairs.** This is the ADR-0012 approval-gate principle applied to the project's own development loop rather than to the agent's value layer.

- **Code**: `scripts/weekly-pipeline.sh`, `scripts/weekly-analysis.sh`, `.claude/skills/weekly-report/`, `.claude/skills/weekly-gate/`, `cli/schedule.py` (`--weekly-pipeline`, `--watchdog`, `--weekly-backup`)
- **ADR**: ADR-0098 (single-session redesign, triage delegation), ADR-0085 (the original chain, partially superseded), ADR-0040 (weekly analysis), ADR-0012 (approval gate)

## Why judge distilled patterns after producing them rather than deciding up front? (ADR-0084)

Distill had been emitting a **near-constant quota**: over ~1,700 live episodes the patterns-per-episode median was 2.00, only 0.1% of episodes returned zero, and the daily rate stayed flat at 1.82–2.18 — output volume tracking activity rather than learning. The obvious repair, tightening `distill_episode.md`, was rejected on measurement: every rewrite moved the abstain rate and the output register together, so tuning the prompt traded one defect for another. The decision instead **relocates the verdict**. `distill_episode.md` is left byte-unchanged, and a post-distill durability gate (`config/prompts/distill_postgate.md`, `distill._postgate`) receives the episode plus its numbered patterns after `_is_valid_pattern` and returns which to keep — **per pattern**, so a two-pattern episode with one grounded pattern keeps one. The ordering is the load-bearing part: asking the same durability question *before* distilling answers "durable" 40/40 with zero gate faults, because naming a worthwhile moment costs nothing when you never have to write it. **Producing the pattern is the evidence requirement**, so the judge must hold the artifact. Offline A/B replay over one fixed 40-episode set whose baseline arm reproduced production: 74 → 59 patterns, judged abstain 0% → 5%.

- **Code**: `core/distill.py` (`_postgate`), `config/prompts/distill_postgate.md`
- **ADR**: ADR-0084 (post-distill durability gate), ADR-0060 (per-episode grounded distill), ADR-0072 (the prompt-side interventions this one declines to extend)
- **Skill**: `.claude/skills/llm-pipeline-layering` (splitting a small model's work by kind *and* by order)

## What counts as "finished" for this project? (ADR-0080)

The end state is defined **per layer**, not as a capability target — what the agent *becomes* is deliberately left undefined, and what can be defined is when the experimental apparatus counts as finished. For the **mechanism layer** (code), completion means the layer *stops moving*: changes become repair-only and mechanism-layer ADRs approach zero. The metaphor is stopping work on the telescope in order to observe with it, and the instrument / audit / chaos-TDD line (ADR-0071 → ADR-0075 → ADR-0077) is already movement toward "trustworthy enough not to touch". A 2026-08-26 amendment makes this operative as a necessary condition: while the feedback loop with the environment (episodes → patterns → skills → selection → generation → back to the environment) does not self-regulate without the owner's or the assistant's routine involvement, the mechanism layer is not finished — human approval gates remain as authority, but their load approaches zero (sufficiency stays a human judgment). The same amendment adds a **metabolic-quality clause**: frequency alone cannot judge value, so the intake must distinguish value along multiple axes (e.g. novelty, importance, the environment's response — the list deliberately open), never reduced to a single scalar. For the **value layer** (constitution, identity, skills, rules), there is no stopping point: that layer is the thing being observed, and its continued motion is the result, not a backlog. The definition is deliberately **not reducible to a benchmark score** — a benchmark would define completion in terms of a capability target, which is exactly what this ADR declines to do.

- **ADR**: ADR-0080 (north star — per-layer end-state definition)
- **Doc**: [docs/CYCLES.md](docs/CYCLES.md) (the nine cycles that drive the project, with their heartbeats and human gates)

## How is the quality of the LLM's own output measured, and how is the backend contract kept honest? (ADR-0088 / ADR-0089)

Two measurement layers added in v2.10.0 close the same class of gap from two sides. **ADR-0089** adds a top-level `evals/` layer (on DeepEval) that measures what `generate_comment()` actually produces: production-parity generation over a 12-case golden dataset (4 axioms × normal/edge/adversarial) under **pinned prompt-asset snapshots**, judged by an isolated `claude -p` against the snapshot constitution into **named verdicts** — binary checks kept as evidence, never aggregated into a score — with regressions detected as per-case verdict transitions against an approved baseline. It sits deliberately outside `verify.sh` (slow, stochastic, delta-judged) and outside `tests/` (conftest kills unmocked LLM calls); `evals/check_staleness.py` mechanically detects when the approved baseline no longer matches the tree and surfaces that as a warning while the decision to re-run stays human. **ADR-0088** makes the `LLMBackend` Protocol checkable by the party with the motive to check it: five Protocol changes had accumulated over three months without reaching either sibling backend repo, so the conformance kit ships **inside the wheel** (`contemplative_agent.testing`, stdlib + `core.llm` imports only, pytest-independent) and is run from main at release time — `python -m contemplative_agent.testing --backend pkg.mod:Name` or `./scripts/check-sibling-backends.sh`.

- **Code**: `evals/` (runner, judge adapter, staleness check), `src/contemplative_agent/testing/`, `scripts/check-sibling-backends.sh`
- **ADR**: ADR-0089 (behavioral eval layer), ADR-0088 (shipped conformance kit), ADR-0087 / ADR-0066 (the backend seam being conformance-checked)
- **Runbook**: [docs/runbooks/sibling-backend-conformance.md](docs/runbooks/sibling-backend-conformance.md)

## What does the human at the constitution-amendment gate see besides a text diff? (ADR-0090)

Since v2.10.0: a behavioral reading. `amend-constitution` is the deepest value-layer intervention the agent performs on itself, and until ADR-0090 its human approval gate (ADR-0012) had exactly two pieces of material — the text diff and trust. The **IPD two-arm bench** (`scripts/ipd-two-arm.sh` + `scripts/ipd_two_arm_report.py`) runs the current constitution and the staged amendment as two arms of the same iterated-prisoner's-dilemma bench and prints the comparison; a **null-pair calibration** (the same constitution in both arms, run twice) measures the bench's own noise floor so a between-arm difference smaller than the bench's noise is not mistaken for a behavioral change. The instrument is read-only with respect to the runtime — nothing under `core/` / `adapters/` / `cli/` changes — and its report carries an audit-hash check tying it to the exact arms it read. The first live use is recorded in the ADR: the 2026-08-09 amendment was adopted with the two-arm reading and the null-pair calibration in hand. Evidence (both arms' raw JSON, the null runs, provenance) lives under `docs/evidence/adr-0090/`, and the amendment procedure is a runbook (`docs/runbooks/constitution-amendment.md`).

- **Code**: `scripts/ipd-two-arm.sh`, `scripts/ipd_two_arm_report.py`, `tests/test_ipd_two_arm_report.py`
- **ADR**: ADR-0090 (IPD two-arm bench), ADR-0012 (the approval gate it feeds), ADR-0071 (the instrument-before-intervention lineage)
- **Evidence**: [docs/evidence/adr-0090/](docs/evidence/adr-0090/)

---

## What is the shadow constitution, and what does it add to the amendment gate? (ADR-0092)

Since v2.11.0: a second reading that does not depend on the model reading its own constitution. `contemplative-agent shadow-constitution` runs the same `constitutional`-view retrieval as `amend-constitution` but with a prompt that never shows the live constitution text; the model synthesizes a constitution from the stored patterns alone, and the instrument records the cosine between that shadow and the live text in `logs/constitution-shadow.jsonl`. It is observe-only: nothing is written to the value layer, and the command is safe against a production `MOLTBOOK_HOME`. The reading answers "what would the agent's own accumulated patterns say its constitution is, if nobody told it?", and the distance between that and the live text is material for the next amendment decision. Calibration anchors (unrelated-text cosine 0.42–0.49, same-genre band) are recorded so a single number can be placed on a scale. ADR-0091 sits beside it: `scripts/value_layer_due_check.py` reads the audit log, the knowledge store, and the staging directory and emits one JSON reading of which value-layer work is due, so the weekly chain stages the monthly identity distill automatically and the Saturday packet carries the due readings; amendments remain a deliberate human event.

- **Code**: `core/constitution_shadow.py`, `cli/` (`shadow-constitution` subcommand), `scripts/value_layer_due_check.py`, `tests/test_constitution_shadow.py`
- **ADR**: ADR-0092 (shadow constitution), ADR-0091 (value-layer cadence), ADR-0090 (IPD bench), ADR-0076 (the shadow-instrument form)
- **Evidence**: [docs/evidence/adr-0092/](docs/evidence/adr-0092/)

---

## What happened to the task ledger between ADR-0094 and ADR-0095?

ADR-0094 (2026-08-14) built a three-layer task ledger: a store (one Markdown file per task, frontmatter `state:`), an append-only journal, and a rendered projection table, with a weekly-chain stage that watched ledger conditions. Two days later ADR-0095 retired everything that parsed: the projection renderer, the scan, the migration, `TASKS.md`, weekly stage 6c, and the `ledger_watch_fired` metric. The machinery had reached about 5,000 lines in two days and was filing its own bugs into the ledger it rendered. What remains is the store (`.notes/tasks/T-XXX.md`) and a global `claims.py` for parallel sessions (claim / release / spawn with a 24-hour lease). ADR-0094 is kept, superseded, as the record of why. The same ADR writes down the filing rule that came out of the episode: review findings outside a commit's diff are filed only at HIGH severity and above, and only after the producer-to-sink path has been quoted with `file:line`; everything else goes into the commit message and is dropped. Bloated ledgers are solved by archiving, not by mechanism.

- **Code**: `~/.claude/scripts/claims.py` (harness-side), `.notes/tasks/` (gitignored store)
- **ADR**: ADR-0095 (retire), ADR-0094 (superseded), ADR-0093 (the repo-plane intake whose ledger-watch half was removed)
- **Evidence**: [docs/evidence/adr-0094/](docs/evidence/adr-0094/)
